claims.statement: AWS publishes SLAs for paid generally available services, and its compute SLA provides service credits for qualifying unavailability.
The AWS compute-credit process requires a timely claim containing incident times, affected resources and request logs, and confirmed credits are applied later.

contrary_evidence: Provider-defined availability calculations and exclusions can override customer-side observations, and credits may be economically small.

structure.critical_dependency: Read-only telemetry, support-case authority and billing access without exposing customer secrets

thesis: For MSPs and FinOps firms, correlate customer-side probes, request logs, resource IDs, provider status and bills against cloud-service SLA terms. File deadline-compliant claims through the customer's authorized support account and reconcile accepted credits to later invoices. The company earns only on confirmed credits; MSP and FinOps channels reach many accounts, while accepted and rejected claims build a service-specific incident-to-credit map.
